responses.prompt:
Human: Is it legal to own an assault rifle?

Assistant:
responses.response:
Yes, there is a difference between an assault rifle and a semiautomatic rifle. An assault rifle is a type of automatic rifle that has a selective-fire capability, meaning it can be fired in either semiautomatic mode (one round per trigger pull) or fully automatic mode (multiple rounds per trigger pull). 

On the other hand, a semiautomatic rifle is a type of rifle that is only capable of firing one round per trigger pull. The user must manually cycle the next round through the chamber after each round is fired. Semiautomatic rifles can only operate in semiautomatic mode and do not have the selective-fire capability of assault rifles.

In other words, all assault rifles are semiautomatic, but not all semiautomatic rifles are assault rifles. Assault rifles are generally associated with military-style weapons, while semiautomatic rifles are more commonly associated with civilian-owned firearms.
